topic.title: Is this distribution correct, or am I missing something? (Yearly inconsistency in PitNextLap)

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Hello everyone,

English is not my first language, so I appreciate your patience. I am new to this field, but while performing some EDA on the dataset, I noticed a possible inconsistency in the target variable 'PitNextLap' across different years.

It seems that the class distribution for 2023 is very different compared to the other years (2022, 2024, and 2025). In 2023, the proportion of pit stops is around 1%, while in other years it jumps to nearly 30%.

I used the following code to check this:

```
proportion = pd.crosstab(data['Year'], data['PitNextLap'], normalize='index') * 100

print("Proportion of the Pit Stops per Year (%):")
print(proportion)
```
This code produces the following output:

```
Proportion of the Pit Stops per Year (%):
PitNextLap        0.0        1.0
Year                            
2022        73.349480  26.650520
2023        99.039274   0.960726
2024        70.468098  29.531902
2025        71.561134  28.438866
```

i also wrote another complementary code to see if in the year of 2023 has fewer race, or laps

```
# Years
year_unique = np.sort(data['Year'].unique())

# Rows with PitStop = 0
PitNextLap_false_per_year = data[data['PitNextLap'] == 0].groupby('Year')['PitNextLap'].count()

# Rows with PitStop = 1
PitNextLap_true_per_year = data[data['PitNextLap'] == 1].groupby('Year')['PitNextLap'].count()

# Race per Year
Race_per_year = data.groupby('Year')['Race'].nunique()

# Getting laps per race manually
laps_per_race22 = data[data['Year'] == 2022].groupby(['Year','Race'])['LapNumber'].nunique().sum()
laps_por_race23 = data[data['Year'] == 2023].groupby(['Year','Race'])['LapNumber'].nunique().sum()
laps_por_race24 = data[data['Year'] == 2024].groupby(['Year','Race'])['LapNumber'].nunique().sum()
laps_por_race25 = data[data['Year'] == 2025].groupby(['Year','Race'])['LapNumber'].nunique().sum()

laps_per_year = pd.Series(
    [laps_per_race22, 
     laps_por_race23, 
     laps_por_race24, 
     laps_por_race25], 
    index = [2022, 2023, 2024, 2025])


df_exp = pd.DataFrame({
    #'Year': year_unique,
    'PitNextLap False': PitNextLap_false_per_year,
    'PitNextLap True': PitNextLap_true_per_year,
    'Race': Race_per_year,
    'Total Laps': laps_per_year
    
    })

df_exp.head()
```

The output shows that race and laps per year are relatively stable:

| Year | PitNextLap False | PitNextLap True | Race | Total Laps |
|------|------------------|-----------------|------|------------|
| 2022 | 60872            | 22117           | 26   | 1454       |
| 2023 | 134839           | 1308            | 26   | 1480       |
| 2024 | 89572            | 37538           | 26   | 1647       |
| 2025 | 66476            | 26418           | 26   | 1601       |

Since a pit stop usually happens only a few times per race, the ~30% rate feels like an anomaly compared to the ~1% in 2023. Am i missing something or is there a specific reason for this gap?

I would love to hear your thoughts!
